long_biography.plain_text:
Papantonio earned an advertising degree from the University of Florida and a law degree from Cumberland School of Law, then worked as a Florida prosecutor. After joining Levin Papantonio, he moved from family and personal-injury cases into asbestos and other mass torts. He built a practice around claims involving drugs, medical devices, toxic contamination and corporate misconduct.

He helped launch Mass Torts Made Perfect in 2000 as a national forum for plaintiffs’ lawyers and later held leadership roles in major opioid and environmental litigation. His courtroom record brought induction into America’s Trial Lawyer Hall of Fame. Outside litigation, Papantonio founded the syndicated Ring of Fire radio programme, hosted America’s Lawyer, appeared in documentaries and wrote both legal instruction and a continuing series of legal thrillers.
